question.problem: Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables, and suppose $\text{E}[X∣Y]=\sqrt{3}\,Y+1.$ If $\text{E}[Y]=\sqrt{3},$ what is $\text{E}[X]?$
question.worked_solution:
We are given an expression for $\text{E}[X∣Y]$ in terms of $Y,$ and we are asked to compute $\text{E}[X].$ This is a direct application of the tower property, which states that

$$
\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[\text{E}[X∣Y]].
$$

So, we substitute the given expression for the inner expectation:

$$
\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[\sqrt{3}\,Y+1]
$$

Now, we apply the linearity of expectation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =\text{E}[\sqrt{3}\,Y+1] \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot \text{E}[Y]+\text{E}[1] \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{3}+1 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
